summary: IDS feed s152_double is degraded: 79% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% IDS tolerance and 2.6% of frames exceed 1518B MTU and are dropped by IDS NIC.

findings.root_cause: 79% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) with no broker-side decryption or clear-text feed, exceeding IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is forwarded as-is from TAP/SPAN without SSL visibility.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature matching but cannot inspect encrypted payloads; detection coverage is severely reduced and encrypted C2/exfiltration will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs clear-text payload; add SSL visibility/decryption at packet broker or mirror already-decrypted traffic to this IDS feed, respecting privacy/policy controls.

findings.root_cause: Upstream network/broker is delivering jumbo/encapsulated frames up to 8058 bytes to a 1 Gbps IDS port limited to 1518 bytes. 63 of 2403 frames (2.6%) exceed MTU and are dropped by the NIC.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently drops 2.6% of frames, creating a blind spot; attackers can evade detection using large frames. Slicing/trimming is not viable because this IDS needs full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Do not slice - IDS needs full payload. Enable jumbo-frame support on IDS NIC/port or normalize MTU/strip encapsulation upstream so frames fit 1518B without truncation.
